evidence.strategic_fidelity: The portfolio correctly targets 기술선도 by selecting low-TRL (TRL 1) exploratory technologies with long development horizons and high uncertainty scores, and the 2030 reference year allows extended R&D runway; the mix of cathode and functional materials reflects a research-heavy orientation consistent with technology leadership.
evidence.competitive_awareness: All three selected technologies fall squarely within the Cathode Materials / Functional Materials domain, demonstrating strong domain fit; high-nickel polycrystalline, LiFSI electrolyte chemistry, and silicon anode materials are all strategically relevant and adjacent technology segments where a cathode materials company can leverage existing competencies.
evidence.market_timing: For 기술선도 strategy, completing 1-2 years before boom is ideal; TECH-001 completes 0.75yr after boom (slight miss), TECH-002 and TECH-004 complete ~1yr after boom — these are modest post-boom completions rather than preemptive, but the errors are within acceptable range and not severely late relative to boom windows.
evidence.patent_market_convergence: The selections are plausible convergence-zone candidates (all have high market_opp scores of 4-5), but there is no explicit evidence in the roadmap that patent activity signals were cross-referenced with market growth data to deliberately target convergence zones; the alignment appears partially coincidental.

weaknesses: TRL progression is critically unrealistic — all three technologies must advance from TRL 1 to deployment-ready in 2-4 years, which is infeasible under normal materials R&D timelines

missing_technologies: Mid-TRL bridging cathode technology (TRL 4-6) to ensure near-term revenue while long-horizon bets mature
Solid-state electrolyte or polymer electrolyte materials to complement LiFSI chemistry and strengthen the functional materials portfolio
Manganese-rich or LMFP cathode materials as a lower-uncertainty complement to the high-nickel bet
investment_issues: Assigning Strategic tier to a TRL 1 technology with executability=1.0 concentrates maximum budget on the highest-risk, lowest-readiness asset without intermediate milestones to validate progress
